The interview blamed cost. The headlines blamed AI.

25 / 30
What he saidWhat was reported
Cost was weighted too heavily, and quality fellAI had failed
A pilot of two new agentsA hiring spree
Headcount to keep falling, to about 2,500A reversal on AI

He calls the original article balanced. His objection is to the headline and what was built on it.

Fifteen months later the chief executive gave an interview that became a cautionary tale. His actual words were that cost had been too predominant a factor, and that what you end up with is lower quality. Read carefully, he is describing how outsourced support had been organised. He is not saying the AI assistant produced poor quality work.

The same article described a pilot of two people, and forecast headcount falling further to about two thousand five hundred. Within ten days the story had become a reversal, a hiring spree, and an admission that AI had failed. One outlet added customer dissatisfaction while citing another outlet rather than the interview. He has pushed back five times in ten months, and the company denied it on the record. He is careful about what he blames. He says the original article was balanced and he will not blame the journalist. His objection is to the headline and to what was built on top of it.
